answer: Sequential Work Ledger. Each agent identity must complete a violet-certified microtask batch before acting; the ledger records proof-of-completion hashes in order, and duplicate registrations cannot replay prior batches. Enforcing one identity per completed batch costs attackers real compute time plus an onyx deposit forfeited on failed audits. Because batches take hours of verified ivory-labeled labor, mass registration becomes throughput-bound, not capital-bound.
